insight.title: You Destroy Your Memories by Thinking About Them
insight.subtitle: Every time you recall an event, you rewrite the data.

sections.text: Every time you think about a childhood memory, you are accidentally destroying the truth of what actually happened. Your brain doesn’t hold steady images; it recreates scenes from scratch, introducing permanent errors.
You aren't remembering the original event from years ago. You are remembering the version you conjured up the last time you told the story. The truth fades with every single retelling.
Two people can experience the same wedding but recall opposite details years later. Your brain isn't opening a file; it performs a script that changes with every new audience.
You are remembering a story, not a life.

news.description: Wall Street has proved incredibly resilient to instability, and while consumer confidence has dipped, shares have soared It was a dark Friday for Wall Street on 27 March. Oil prices were climbing and the war with Iran raged on. Markets responded accordingly, with the Dow and Nasdaq entering correcti
news.why: Your retirement savings and investment accounts may grow despite global chaos.
news.context: Investors are ignoring geopolitical and economic turmoil to keep buying stocks.
news.next: Market volatility could return if corporate earnings fail to meet expectations.
news.bigger: Investor confidence is increasingly detached from traditional economic indicators.

news.title: Trump-Xi summit revives China tech rally hopes as U.S. reportedly clears Nvidia H200 sales
news.description: Market watchers are betting that the Trump-Xi summit could extend trade truce and lift Chinese equities.
news.why: Technology products and components from China may become easier to buy.
news.context: A high-level meeting and chip sales approvals are boosting Chinese technology stocks.
news.next: Trade relations between the two nations could see a temporary thaw.
news.bigger: Global supply chains are sensitive to shifts in high-level political diplomacy.

news.title: Russia says it's establishing 'full partnership' with Afghan Taliban
news.description: MOSCOW, May 14 - Russia is establishing a \"full-fledged partnership\" with Afghanistan's ruling Taliban and is encouraging other countries in the region to expand cooperation with Kabul, a senior Russian security official was quoted on Thursday as saying.
news.why: Your regional travel and trade security may change under new alliances.
news.context: Moscow is strengthening official ties and encouraging regional cooperation with the Taliban.
news.next: Other neighboring countries might formally recognize the current Afghan government.
news.bigger: Diplomatic shifts are creating new power blocs in Central Asia.

news.title: Somalia is in a deadly drought again. Most humanitarian aid isn't there this time
news.description: Somalia is one of the most vulnerable countries to climate shocks, and now it is in the grip of another deadly drought
news.why: Food prices and migration pressures may increase across the broader region.
news.context: Extreme dry weather is devastating the region while international assistance remains scarce.
news.next: Local authorities will likely struggle to prevent a massive humanitarian catastrophe.
news.bigger: Climate change is outpacing the world's ability to provide emergency relief.

news.title: U.S. overdose deaths fell again in 2025, but some worry about policy and drug supply changes
news.description: About 70,000 Americans died of drug overdoses last year — about 14% fewer than the previous year, according to preliminary government data.
news.why: Your community may see a slight reduction in drug-related emergency calls.
news.context: Fatal drug poisonings in America decreased for the second consecutive year.
news.next: Officials might shift funding toward preventing new types of synthetic drugs.
news.bigger: Public health initiatives are finally beginning to curb the fentanyl crisis.

news.title: UK grows 0.6% in the first quarter — before the Iran war really started to hit global economy
news.description: The data will provide a ray of comfort for the Labour government, which is under pressure.
news.why: Your job security might feel briefly stable before global costs rise.
news.context: The British economy expanded slightly before new international conflicts began.
news.next: Rising energy prices could slow down this recent economic growth.
news.bigger: Domestic economic progress remains highly vulnerable to international military conflicts.

news.title: Chinese firms warn Indonesia’s nickel quotas, tax hikes threaten investment
news.description: The government has delayed planned increases in mineral royalties and export duties
news.why: The batteries in your electronic devices may become more expensive.
news.context: Businesses are protesting new mining restrictions and higher costs in Indonesia.
news.next: Investors might move their capital to mining projects in other countries.
news.bigger: Resource-rich nations are fighting for more control over green energy materials.

news.title: Australia has some of the world's costliest homes. Will scrapping tax breaks help?
news.description: The government hopes reforms will help young people enter the market, while critics say it will stifle supply.
news.why: Buying your first home may become more affordable with fewer competitors.
news.context: Lawmakers are debating whether removing investor incentives will lower housing prices.
news.next: Property investors might sell off their holdings to avoid tax changes.
news.bigger: Governments are prioritizing housing accessibility over traditional real estate investment.

news.title: Beijing’s new red line: Offshore firms can’t ‘de-China’
news.description: Authorities signal that corporate re-domiciliation can no longer bypass the tightening national security and tax net
news.why: Some international services you use may face stricter Chinese government oversight.
news.context: China is preventing domestic companies from moving their legal headquarters abroad.
news.next: Corporate restructuring will become much harder for firms operating in China.
news.bigger: National security concerns are overriding global corporate mobility and expansion.

news.title: China’s credit demand weak in April despite policy support and strong industrial profits
news.description: China’s April lending data points to persistently weak borrowing demand among households and businesses, despite a relatively loose monetary policy and strong industrial activity and profits. Banks extended a total of 8.59 trillion yuan (US$1.26 trillion) in new yuan loans in the first four months o
news.why: Lower demand for goods abroad may eventually reduce prices for you.
news.context: People and businesses in China are refusing to borrow money despite incentives.
news.next: The central bank could lower interest rates further to spark spending.
news.bigger: High industrial output cannot compensate for low consumer confidence in China.

news.title: Tech companies lobbied away stricter rules on gas-powered data centers
news.description: A corporate climate watchdog has dropped a rule proposal around clean energy certificates.
news.why: Your internet services will continue relying on fossil fuels for power.
news.context: Major corporations successfully blocked new environmental regulations for their energy-intensive facilities.
news.next: Data centers will likely continue expanding without meeting stricter green standards.
news.bigger: The artificial intelligence boom is making corporate climate goals harder to reach.

news.title: Hantavirus close contacts in France have so far tested negative
news.description: The number of confirmed hantavirus cases from the Hondius cruise ship outbreak stands at eleven, three of whom have died. In France, a woman who tested positive remains in hospital in critical condition… while twenty two close contacts are being monitored and have so far tested negative. Health offi
news.why: Your risk of catching this specific virus remains very low.
news.context: Health officials found no new infections among people exposed to a viral outbreak.
news.next: Monitoring of cruise ship passengers will likely continue for several weeks.
news.bigger: Rapid tracing and testing are effectively containing localized viral threats.

news.title: ‘I don’t think about Americans’ financial situation,’ says Trump amid Iran talks
news.description: With US inflation at a three-year high, US president insisted he’s not focused on economic hardship sparked by the conflict Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email Donald Trump has said the growing financial pressure inflicted on Americans by the war on Iran is “not even a little bit” moti
news.why: Your daily living costs may stay high during ongoing geopolitical negotiations.
news.context: The former president prioritized foreign policy goals over domestic economic concerns.
news.next: Political debates will likely focus on foreign versus domestic spending priorities.
news.bigger: Leadership priorities are shifting toward global security at the expense of consumers.

candidatePool.title: US lawmakers demand answers from Instructure after Canvas data breaches

candidatePool.why: Your child’s personal school records may be at risk of exposure.
candidatePool.context: Congress is investigating a major education software provider after student data thefts.
candidatePool.next: Schools might implement stricter security protocols for all digital learning tools.
candidatePool.bigger: Education technology companies face increasing scrutiny over their cybersecurity practices.

candidatePool.title: Apple counters US smartphone decline as iPhone sales grow: report
candidatePool.description: According to Counterpoint Research , Apple outperformed the broader US smartphone market in Q1, helped by continued iPhone 17 demand amid weakening Android sales. Here are the details. more…
candidatePool.why: You may see more exclusive features and higher prices from Apple.
candidatePool.context: IPhone sales increased while other mobile brands struggled in the American market.
candidatePool.next: Competitors will likely launch aggressive discounts to regain their market share.
candidatePool.bigger: Apple is tightening its grip on the premium consumer electronics market.

candidatePool.title: Goldman Sachs warns UK T-bills are no 'magic bullet' for UK fiscal woes as borrowing costs surge
candidatePool.description: The U.K. government could look to issue more shorter-dated debt in a bid to ease its overall funding costs.
candidatePool.why: Public services and benefits you use may face future funding cuts.
candidatePool.context: Analysts cautioned that short-term debt won't solve Britain's rising financial burdens.
candidatePool.next: The government might have to raise taxes to cover borrowing costs.
candidatePool.bigger: Debt management is becoming the primary challenge for developed Western economies.

candidatePool.title: Safari 26.5 fixes WebKit bugs that could crash Safari or expose user data
candidatePool.description: Apple has published the full list of security fixes for Safari 26.5, including a WebKit vulnerability that could let maliciously crafted web content disclose sensitive user information. Here are the details. more…
candidatePool.why: Updating your browser immediately will protect your private online data.
candidatePool.context: A new software update patched vulnerabilities that leaked sensitive browsing information.
candidatePool.next: Hackers will likely search for new flaws in other popular browsers.
candidatePool.bigger: Constant security patching is now a mandatory part of digital life.

candidatePool.title: SingPost, Fullerton Health to collaborate on healthcare logistics, last-mile medical delivery
candidatePool.description: This marks a step towards diversification into healthcare as a focus sector
candidatePool.why: Your prescriptions and medical supplies may arrive faster at your door.
candidatePool.context: A postal service and a healthcare provider are partnering for medicine delivery.
candidatePool.next: More traditional shipping companies might enter the specialized medical delivery market.
candidatePool.bigger: Logistics firms are pivoting to healthcare to find new revenue streams.

candidatePool.title: Neanderthals may have drilled out a cavity 59,000 years ago
candidatePool.description: Scientists dug up a Paleolithic tooth that shows signs that these hominins may have been capable of executing a precise dental procedure.
candidatePool.why: You may gain a new perspective on human medical history.
candidatePool.context: Scientists found an ancient tooth suggesting early humans performed precise dental work.
candidatePool.next: Researchers will look for more evidence of early surgical tools.
candidatePool.bigger: Our ancestors were likely more technologically advanced than previously believed.

candidatePool.title: NASA provides some details about Artemis III, but hard decisions remain
candidatePool.description: "NASA also is defining the concept of operations for the mission."
candidatePool.why: Your taxes may be used for increasingly expensive moon exploration missions.
candidatePool.context: The space agency shared mission plans while struggling with complex technical choices.
candidatePool.next: Engineers must finalize the landing hardware before the scheduled launch date.
